mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) rising by more than 0.4 percentage points from the previous month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the negative rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both personal savings (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% from the previous month signals a sharp contraction in household demand and investment, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered months, or the negative rank IC is below 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid monthly decline in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points signals an emergency monetary easing in response to a financial shock, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the positive rank IC is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a statistical artifact of labor force reclassification rather than real job growth; this regime typically precedes weak equity performance, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the negative rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for four consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which increases the probability of aggressive central bank tightening and ultimately produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY change > 4% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.03.
